archetype: Aristocrats-combo, and strategic_frame.json's 'combo' label holds — the audit's archetype overrides (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6) fit. But the deck the thirteen checker-passed stacks describe is NOT the one goldfish_targets.json declares. The targets declare four kills built around Nest of Scarabs, Blowfly Infestation, Carnifex Demon and Mikaeus. What the checker has actually signed is a Gravecrawler recursion deck: stacks 009 and 011 (both pass) are self-funding unbounded drains that name neither the commander, nor Nest of Scarabs, nor Blowfly Infestation, and 012 (pass) is a two-card mandatory loop that names none of them either. The frame is right; the declared engine is a generation behind the evidence.
verdict: It functions, it turns over its enablers, and — new on this evidence — it converts. Thirteen checker-passed stacks now include three self-funding kills the checker calls unbounded (009 Warren Soultrader + Gravecrawler + Bastion of Remembrance, 011 Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar + a Zombie + Bastion, 012 Exquisite Blood + South Wind Avatar) plus one library-bounded lethal loop with 20-25 activations of margin (010 Mikaeus + Yawgmoth). The previous verdict — that the deck does not convert — was drawn from eight stacks, five of which resolved the same bounded Nest of Scarabs engine; it does not survive the new set. What limits the deck now is that every one of those kills is a small pile of permanents assembled on the battlefield in a deck that cannot remove a permanent. interaction-breadth measures 1 class answered against a target of 5, a regex sweep of all 79 maindeck oracle texts returns zero cards that destroy or exile a noncreature permanent, and two of the three unbounded kills cast Gravecrawler out of the graveyard.

open_questions.question: Does stack 009's loop stay unbounded and lethal with Zulaport Cutthroat, Blood Artist or Ayara, First of Locthwain in Bastion of Remembrance's slot? combo_details records all four as separate Infinite lifeloss lines and only Bastion has been resolved.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether Bastion is a single point of failure across three verified kills or the verified member of a four-wide any_of. That is the difference between a 0.071 component and a 0.258 one, and it changes what you tutor for.

open_questions.question: Does The Meathook Massacre substitute for Bastion of Remembrance inside stack 009's loop? Meathook has the each-opponent trigger and the enchantment body, and its lifegain trigger fires only when a creature an OPPONENT controls dies — 009's four opponents control no permanents — while 009's per-iteration ledger has you paying 1 life to Warren Soultrader and Bastion refunding it.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Add candidate 4 is prescribed as a Bastion closer. If the life ledger breaks the loop, it is a sweeper and a second drain but not redundancy for the deck's most load-bearing card, and the ranking should change.

open_questions.question: Is Exquisite Blood + Marauding Blight-Priest (and + Starscape Cleric) lethal in a four-opponent pod on the same terms stack 012 established for South Wind Avatar, given neither has the Avatar's own 'another creature you control dies' lifegain trigger to start the loop?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both adds are prescribed on 012's shape. The ignition differs — the Avatar starts its own loop, the other two need an external lifegain event — and that difference is exactly the kind a scenario exists to catch.

open_questions.question: Does the single-target penalty stacks 003 and 004 measured (8 pod life versus 28) survive onto an UNBOUNDED loop? On a self-funding line the iteration count is the pilot's choice, so a 'target player loses 1' drain may kill four seats sequentially at four times the iterations rather than at a quarter of the reach.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the single most-quoted piloting fact in this deck's artifacts and it was measured only on a bounded engine. If it does not transfer, Blood Artist stops being a liability and the drain class is six wide rather than three.

open_questions.question: Should goldfish_targets.json be rewritten against the verified set? It declares four kills, one of which (THE SECOND KILL) names Carnifex Demon as a required middle that stack 010 verified without, and it does not declare stack 011's Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar + a Zombie + a drain line at all.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every assembly rate in this diagnosis is measured against declarations that the checker has now overtaken. The audit cannot express the union of four kills, but it can at least be measuring the right four.

open_questions.question: Does adding Culling the Weak to the 'Fast mana' any_of move the 0.435, and should the any_of also carry Jet Medallion and the deck's 14 one-drops as the enabling condition? goldfish explicitly does not model cost reducers or rituals beyond the three named cards.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the thinnest measured component in the deck and the only one no add on this list demonstrably closes. Without the measurement, add candidate 7 is a preference.

open_questions.question: Does Drivnod, Carnage Dominus double Bastion of Remembrance inside stack 009's loop — and if the loop is already unbounded, does doubling buy anything at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The coach ranks Drivnod fourth on the strength of doubling Bastion on stack 002's bounded board. On an unbounded loop a multiplier is worth nothing, so the card's value depends entirely on which family it is being bought for — and no artifact currently says which.

open_questions.question: Does Black Sun's Zenith at X greater than 1 make Nest of Scarabs produce X Insects per creature? Stack 013 states the arithmetic as a consequence of its reading and explicitly declines to resolve it, naming the missing case: multiple counters per creature in one event, on every creature on the battlefield rather than only yours.
open_questions.why_it_matters: 013 says in as many words that the cut-candidacy question for Black Sun's Zenith should be settled by a scenario that actually resolves a Zenith. CORRECTED this pass: it is NOT the deck's only scalable wipe after Carnifex leaves. The sweeper set then reads Black Sun's Zenith, Soul Snuffers and Toxic Deluge, plus The Meathook Massacre if that add lands — Toxic Deluge ('pay X life ... all creatures get -X/-X') and Meathook ({X}{B}{B}, 'each creature gets -X/-X') both scale, and Soul Snuffers is the fixed one. The narrower stake is the real one: the Zenith is the only scalable wipe that also FEEDS Nest of Scarabs, so its ceiling decides whether it is a sweeper or half a win condition, and therefore whether it belongs on a cut list at all.

gaps: THE UNION OF FOUR VERIFIED KILLS IS STILL NOT A NUMBER ANYONE HAS. deck-audit says so itself: the target schema is an AND of ORs and cannot express 'any one of four independent kills', and averaging them would invent a figure the simulation never measured. The closest measured proxy, 'EITHER kill assembled', covers only two of the four at 0.055 unassisted / 0.328 assisted. So 'how often does this deck assemble something lethal' is unanswered, and the verdict above is phrased against what the stacks measured rather than against an aggregate that does not exist.

THE PREVIOUS DIAGNOSIS'S CENTRAL INFERENCE IS WITHDRAWN, AND THE SAMPLING CRITIQUE THAT KILLED IT IS ACCEPTED IN FULL. It read 'four declared kills, one verified' as a conversion ceiling. Five of its eight stacks resolved the Yawgmoth + Nest of Scarabs family, which combo_details had already tagged Near-infinite; the truly-infinite family had never been handed to the checker. Stacks 009, 011 and 012 came back unbounded and lethal. The old threat-density verdict of 'weakness' is reversed to 'strength' above, and no prescription on this page rests on the old reading.

TWO PAINFUL CUTS ARE NAMED AND NEITHER IS COMFORTABLE. Blowfly Infestation deletes a checker-passed unbounded LOOP whose lethal configuration stack 001 specifies but which no stack has resolved — 001's own headline is 'REFUTED AS A KILL ON THIS BOARD' — and it orphans stacks 001 and 007; Carnifex Demon removes the deck's only repeatable mass ignition. Both orphans_stack lists are the validator's mechanical 'the scenario names this card' set, and both are narrower as dependencies: Blowfly is on 001's and 007's boards but appears in 009 only as a card its note EXCLUDES, and Carnifex is on no board at all — 013's real board dependency is Necroskitter. THE PLAN-COUNT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN ARTIFACT-WIDE THIS PASS, not only under Blowfly, and the previous version of this gap — which said both cuts were argued from the corpus's cap on unconnected plans — is retracted. The cap reaches none of these cuts: the Blowfly family, the bounded Yawgmoth + Nest family and the self-funding loops all share Nest of Scarabs, the drain class and the ignition class, and the same section names that overlap as the RECONCILIATION of the cap rather than a violation of it. Cutting Carnifex removes one card from a family that survives the cut intact (stacks 002-005, 010, 013), so it reduces no plan count at all. The cap quote has therefore been dropped from the Necroskitter cut, the Carnifex cut and the Nest of Scarabs lean as well as from Blowfly. What each painful cut now rests on is stated in its own entry: Blowfly on the two measured stacks plus the uncovered enchantment class, Carnifex on stack 010 verifying THE SECOND KILL without it and stack 013 measuring its ignition as linear in the board rather than quadratic. Both are recommended anyway. The alternative painful cut considered and REJECTED was Toxic Deluge: the previous diagnosis cut it, deck-skeptic showed the applied list then landed sweepers at 2, and the coach refused it outright. It is the only wipe in the 99 that scales past 4 toughness for three mana, and at {2}{B} it is the cheapest answer to an oversized or indestructible board — Black Sun's Zenith reaches the same boards only at {X}{B}{B}. It stays.

THE 8-VERSUS-28 CONTRAST IS BOUNDED-ENGINE EVIDENCE AND IS NOT GENERALISED HERE. Stacks 003 and 004 measured it on the Yawgmoth + Nest engine, which terminates by body exhaustion. The old diagnosis used it as a general rule about drain selection; this one uses it only as a preference among ADDS and routes the general question to a scenario. Blood Artist is not on the cut list for that reason.

GRAVECRAWLER HAS NO CLOSER AND I LOOKED. The pool candidates the audit and upgrade-facts surface — Nether Traitor, Forsaken Miner, Bloodsoaked Champion, Pawn of Ulamog — each fail for a stated reason: Nether Traitor's return trigger requires ANOTHER creature to die, so it can never be the loop's own sacrifice; Forsaken Miner's is crime-gated and needs an opponent-facing target every iteration; Bloodsoaked Champion's is raid-gated and costs {1}{B}; Pawn of Ulamog reads 'another NONTOKEN creature you control dies'. One sacrifice through Phyrexian Altar or Warren Soultrader refunds exactly one mana, so {B} is the price ceiling and Gravecrawler is the only body that meets it unconditionally. This is a real exposure the pool does not close.

THE ROLE TAXONOMY MISCLASSIFIES FOUR CARDS HERE AND THREE MOVE AN AXIS. Necropotence is filed 'stax' alone, so the best draw engine in mono-black contributes nothing to card-advantage; Bojuka Bog is 'land:tapped', so its graveyard exile is invisible to interaction-breadth (true reading 2, not 1); Supernatural Stamina has no card_roles entry at all and Malakir Rebirth is 'ramp:ritual', and both grant a dies-trigger return, i.e. protection (true reading 5, not 3). The audit's own probe note catches five cards; Necropotence and Bojuka Bog are not among them. The fix is a ROLE_PATTERNS edit plus `manamap card-roles`, not a decklist change, and it is out of scope for a read-only diagnosis.

goldfish_targets.json IS STALE RELATIVE TO THE VERIFIED SET, AND EVERY ENGINE RATE ON THIS PAGE INHERITS THAT. It declares Carnifex Demon as a required middle of THE SECOND KILL, which stack 010 verified without him, and it declares no target at all for stack 011's line. deck-audit's freshness block reports goldfish_metrics.json and mana_analysis.json as current against the decklist sha, so the rates are correctly computed — they are just computed against the wrong declaration. Queued as an open question.

RECON IS DATED AND ITS PERCENTAGES CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED HERE. deck_recon.json carries as_of 2026-08-03 and no artifact in this repo holds per-commander inclusion rates — docs/deck-builder-v2.md names that hole explicitly. Five adds cite it (Urborg, Cabal Coffers, Feed the Swarm, The Meathook Massacre, Culling the Weak) and in every case the recon is corroboration for a card an axis or a component already named; no axis verdict rests on an inclusion percentage.

PRICES ARE STRIPPED from cards.csv, so nothing here weighs acquisition cost. Two of the seven adds are already on this deck's bench (Cabal Coffers, Urborg); the other five are purchases of unknown size.

NOT ONE OF THE 42 CONTAINED COMBO LINES IS VERIFIED BY CONTAINMENT ALONE. Eleven are two-card infinites by Commander Spellbook's tagging and the checker has now both refuted that tagging (stacks 001, 004, 005) and confirmed it (009, 011, 012) on this same deck — which is exactly why containment is not evidence. Every combo line named in an add above carries 'needs a stack scenario'.

THE COACH'S REMAINING PROPOSALS ARE NOT REJECTED, THEY ARE UNPRESCRIBED. Drivnod, Carnage Dominus is queued as an open question because a trigger doubler is worth nothing on an unbounded loop and the case for it was built on stack 002's bounded board. Withering Torment would be a second creature-or-enchantment answer, which the corpus calls doubling before the artifact and land classes are covered. Nadier's Nightblade ('Whenever a token you control leaves the battlefield, each opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life') stays unprescribed, but the reason given in the previous pass was wrong and is withdrawn: 009's loop DOES move a token every iteration — steps 5 and 12 create a Treasure, step 7 sacrifices it to pay Gravecrawler's {B}, and the step-13 ledger records 'Treasures created: 1 ... Treasures sacrificed: 1'. Its trigger condition is therefore met on the face of the text. What no artifact establishes is what that buys on a loop already unbounded, or whether it changes 009's ledger, and that needs its own scenario. Butcher Ghoul survives the cut list by default, not by argument.

APPLYING BOTH RECURSION CUTS TOGETHER IS UNPRICED, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. Phyrexian Reclamation and Nim Deathmantle are both on the cut list at 'contested', and each entry prices its own removal against a 99 that still contains the other. Nothing here prices the pair. If both leave, the only repeatable returns left are self-returns — Gravecrawler ('You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as you control a Zombie') and Reassembling Skeleton ('{1}{B}: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped') — because Persist, Victimize, Animate Dead, Malakir Rebirth, Takenuma and Agadeem's Awakening are one-shots, and gaps[4] already names Gravecrawler as an exposure the pool does not close. Treat the two as alternatives, not as a pair.

findings.note: NEW FINDING, and it is the headline of the page. 'The targets declare four kills built around Nest of Scarabs, Blowfly Infestation, Carnifex Demon and Mikaeus' is false of half the declarations, and the conclusion drawn from it — 'the declared engine is a generation behind the evidence' — is refuted by the deck's own goldfish_targets.json. I read all four kill targets verbatim: (1) 'Both halves of the original kill drawn (Blowfly + Nest)'; (2) 'THE SECOND KILL: Mikaeus + a self-shrinking body + a free sac outlet' with Carnifex Demon as a required middle; (3) 'THE THIRD KILL: Exquisite Blood + a lifegain-triggered drain' = any_of [Exquisite Blood] AND any_of [South Wind Avatar]; (4) 'THE FOURTH KILL: Warren Soultrader + Gravecrawler + any drain' = any_of [Warren Soultrader] AND any_of [Gravecrawler] AND any_of [Ayara, Bastion, Blood Artist, Zulaport]. Targets (3) and (4) name none of the four cards the archetype block says the declarations are built around — and they are EXACTLY the lines stacks 012 and 009 verified. Stack 009's own scenario.extras.note_for_the_resolver settles it in one sentence: 'This is the deck's declared FOURTH KILL and it has never been resolved.' So 009 was declared and unresolved, not undeclared, and 012 resolved a declared target too. The artifact already knows this and says so correctly two thousand words later: gaps[6] scopes the staleness to precisely two things — 'It declares Carnifex Demon as a required middle of THE SECOND KILL, which stack 010 verified without him, and it declares no target at all for stack 011's line' — and open_questions[4] repeats that narrower version. The archetype block is the wide version of a claim the artifact elsewhere states narrowly and correctly, and it is the first thing a pilot reads. The honest sentence is gaps[6]'s: of the four declarations, one middle is falsified (Carnifex in THE SECOND KILL) and one verified line (011) has no declaration; the other two verified kills are declared targets that had simply never been handed to the checker.

NEW FINDING. 'the family stacks 002-005 measured at 8 to 52 pod life against 160' — no stack in 002-005 measured 52. I read all four final_state summaries: 002 'seven creatures you controlled die ... each opponent 40 -> 33, 28 total life removed from a pod of 160' (and 32 on its with-proliferate line, stated there as a property of the line, not the board); 003 'each opponent loses 7 life; 28 total life across the table'; 004 'THE BOARD'S NUMBER IS EIGHT: eight creature deaths ... eight life removed'; 005 'The drain therefore fired 7 times for 1 life per opponent: 28 total opposing life, each opponent 40 -> 33'. The range across 002-005 is 8 to 28 (32 on one named line), not 8 to 52. The 52 is stack 008's figure — Mirkwood Bats + Yawgmoth + Nest, '13 triggers x 4 opponents = 52 life' — and stack 008 is cited NOWHERE in this diagnosis (zero occurrences of '008'). Worse, 008's own checker-passed text forbids exactly this collapse: 'Never present 002, 003 and this stack as one result on one board', giving two structural reasons (a creation-and-sacrifice drainer is paid twice per activation where a death drainer is paid once per body; a 2/3 body absorbs two counters where a 1/1 cannot), and it warns separately that 002's 28 'is not comparable to this line'. The figure is inflated 86% at the top of a range that is load-bearing for a PAINFUL cut: the sentence exists to say the bounded family's ceiling was real before the self-funding loops demoted it, and it overstates that ceiling with a number imported from an uncited stack that says not to import it.

PRIOR FINDING RESOLVED, and I swept for the retraction myself rather than trusting the report. The cap quote 'never more than two *unconnected* ones — cut the least efficient' now appears ZERO times in the artifact (grep -c on the exact string). I enumerated all 42 citation quotes by JSON path: cut_candidates[2] (Necroskitter) carries only deckbuilding.cutting; cut_candidates[6] (Carnifex) carries cutting + the interaction-suite wipe-drift quote; lean_into[3] (Nest) carries threat-density 'Separate ceiling from median...' + cutting — the replacement the doctor reported, and it is verbatim in the section and apt (the claim is that Nest is no longer the one spectacular finisher). The word 'unconnected' survives in exactly two places, both of them the retraction itself (cut_candidates[5].why and gaps[2]), and 'cut the least efficient' appears nowhere. gaps[2] now names the retraction as artifact-wide, states what each painful cut rests on instead (Blowfly on stacks 001 and 007 plus the uncovered enchantment class; Carnifex on 010 verifying THE SECOND KILL without him and 013 measuring his ignition as linear), and reads the section correctly: 'Layering reconciles them: overlap pieces, so five cards support four combos' is indeed the sentence immediately after the cap in strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density, and it is the reconciliation, not a violation. The sweep is clean.

PRIOR FINDING CORRECTED, and the narrowed claim survives an exhaustive check. I regex-swept all 79 maindeck oracle texts for graveyard returns. Repeatable returns in the 99: Nim Deathmantle ('Whenever a nontoken creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield, you may pay {4}' — battlefield, no once-per-turn clause), Reassembling Skeleton ('{1}{B}: Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped' — self, battlefield), Gravecrawler (self-recast), and Phyrexian Reclamation ('{1}{B}, Pay 2 life: Return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand'). One-shots: Persist, Victimize, Animate Dead, Agadeem's Awakening (all battlefield), Malakir Rebirth (dies-trigger return), and Takenuma, Abandoned Mire — the ONLY other graveyard-to-hand route, and its channel discards the card, so it is once. So 'the only repeatable graveyard-to-HAND route' is exactly right, the withdrawn 'only repeatable recursion' sentence is gone, and Nim Deathmantle is named as the counterexample by the entry itself. The double cut is now declared UNPRICED in gaps[11] with the real consequence spelled out (only self-returns left) and the directive 'Take one, not both'. Both halves of my prior finding are closed.

PRIOR FINDING CORRECTED and the count is now right in every place it appears. The entry reads 'This deletes a checker-passed unbounded LOOP whose lethal configuration stack 001 specifies but which no stack has resolved. CORRECTED this pass: it is not a verified kill, and the verified-kill count on this page stays at four (009, 010, 011, 012).' I re-read 001's verdict object field by field: a_loop_unbounded true, a_loop_lethal_on_this_board false, a_iterations_to_zero_on_this_board null, a_total_drain_per_opponent 3, opponents ending at 37, headline 'REFUTED AS A KILL ON THIS BOARD' — every quoted field is exact. The 38 figure is a_iterations_to_zero_with_one_more_creature, and 'one more creature' on this board is precisely build_requirement case (1) (a creature drain plus two other creatures, three total), so attributing 38 to case (1) is correct. gaps[2] carries the same corrected wording. Nothing on the page now counts five verified kills.

PRIOR FINDING CORRECTED. I re-ran manabase.land_colors over every land copy in the maindeck: 35 of 36 produce B and the sole exception is Ancient Tomb ('{T}: Add {C}{C}'), exactly as the entry now states, and mana_analysis.json's sources.total B is 43 (35 land + 8 nonland). Net 43 -> 44, the same number, so the corrected figure survives set application. The entry also keeps its honest framing: colour-sources gap is 0 and taplands gap is 0, so this closes no hole and ranks first to drop.

PRIOR FINDING CORRECTED, and the narrowed stake is the right one. card_roles.json gives removal:sweeper to exactly four maindeck cards — Black Sun's Zenith, Carnifex Demon, Soul Snuffers, Toxic Deluge — matching the audit's 4. After the Carnifex cut the set is Black Sun's Zenith, Soul Snuffers, Toxic Deluge (+ Meathook), which is what the entry now says. Scaling checks out from oracle text: Zenith 'Put X -1/-1 counters on each creature', Toxic Deluge 'pay X life ... All creatures get -X/-X', Meathook '{X}{B}{B} ... each creature gets -X/-X'; Soul Snuffers is fixed at one counter. And the replacement stake is exact: of the three scalable wipes only Black Sun's Zenith places COUNTERS, so it is the only one that feeds Nest of Scarabs — Deluge and Meathook apply -X/-X until end of turn and trigger nothing. The question's attribution to 013's explicit refusal to resolve a Zenith at X>1 is also faithful.

I established the verified-kill count of four independently, in both directions, rather than accepting it. All 13 stacks carry checker.verdict == pass. Lethal on all four seats: 009 ('40 drain events bring a seat to exactly 0 — one has already resolved, so 39 further iterations take all four opponents to 0 at once'), 010 ('All four opponents reach 0 together and leave the game; you are still in it, so you win (104.2a)'), 011 ('39 further iterations put all four opponents at 0 at the same state-based-action check, and you end at 80 life'), 012 ('Not a draw -- you win ... Drain #40 takes all four opponents from 1 to 0 simultaneously'). Not kills, checked one by one so the count is not an undercount either: 001 refuted (drain caps at 3/seat, opponents end at 37); 002 five completed activations, 28 pod life of 160, 'No opponent comes near losing'; 003 28 pod life; 004 'NOT A KILL, AND NOT EVEN CLOSE', 8 life removed; 005 8 activations, 28 opposing life, 'decisively NOT infinite'; 006, 008 and 013 are rules questions with no lethal claim; 007 is an explicit halt. Four is right. Three of the four route through Bastion of Remembrance (009, 010, 011) and 012 does not — the SPOF's 'three of the deck's four verified lethal lines' is exact.

SET CONSISTENCY, checked computationally and not previously checked by either of us.
